```{r setup}
library(golfops)
card <- peoria_rate_card()
open <- dobson_operating_daily()
open <- open[open$rounds_played > 0, ]
weekday <- summarize_golf_rounds(open, by = "weekday", duplicates = "drop_extra")
yield_of <- function(day) {
  weekday$green_fee_per_played_round[as.character(weekday$period) == day]
}
dollars <- function(x) paste0("$", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2))
money <- function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "—", paste0("$", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 0)))
}
one_price <- function(facility, product, segment, day, daypart) {
  hit <- card$price[
    card$facility == facility &
      card$product == product &
      card$segment == segment &
      card$day == day &
      card$daypart == daypart
  ]
  if (length(hit) == 0) NA_real_ else hit[[1]]
}
```

Dobson Ranch published a pricing guide on September 16, 2026, [Dobson Ranch Green Fees Explained](https://www.dobsonranchgolfclub.com/blog/dobson-ranch-green-fees-explained-mesa-az-2026-guide). It is a course editorial page. It points to the City of Mesa fee schedule and to the live checkout at `dobson-ranch.book.teeitup.golf`. The operating extract ends April 30, 2026, so these dollars are later than the rounds in the file.

The guide's adult 18-hole range is $17 to $150, and it says most tee times fall between $39 and $69. Season and time of day are the rows it actually prices. Day of week is named as a driver, with no weekday column. The guide calls the schedule dynamic and also says demand moves the quote. It does not publish the rule that separates those two.

```{r dobson-guide, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
guide <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Snowbird morning, Nov–Apr",
    "Summer or shoulder mid-day",
    "Twilight, about 2 PM",
    "Sunset",
    "Junior, 18 holes",
    "Ranch Card",
    "Smash Pass"
  ),
  `What the guide prints` = c(
    "Adult example $69, range up to $150",
    "Adult example $39, range down to $17",
    "Adult $11–$100, any season",
    "Adult $9–$39, any season",
    "$12–$60",
    "$109 for 2026, $99 for 2027",
    "$24.99 a month, includes the Ranch Card"
  ),
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  guide,
  caption = "Dobson Ranch Golf Club, September 16, 2026. Planning examples and published ranges. The per-round card discount is not on the page."
)
```

The green fee is course access. Cart, clubs, and range balls are separate, and the cart fee is not itemized. Senior, resident, and military rates are not on the page. On played days in the extract, Friday's collected green fee is `r dollars(yield_of("Friday"))` a round and Sunday's is `r dollars(yield_of("Sunday"))`. [Yield per round](dollars-per-golfer.html) is that receipt. The extract has no rate code.

## Peoria

`peoria_rate_card()` is a transcription of a sheet labeled "Peoria weekday and weekend prices, version 2." The original file is not in the package. These are not Dobson Ranch or City of Mesa rates. The sheet key spells Newman as Neuman.

Walking fees are the same on weekdays and weekends. The weekend difference is the adult price that includes a cart. Front nine and back nine carry the same walking and cart-included fees, so each course is one nine-hole row. Twilight is the exception: it is posted on Kellogg Executive, Kellogg Back 9, and Madison Back 9 only.

```{r peoria, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
same_walking <- function(facility) {
  fields <- list(
    c("Adult", "Weekday", "Day"),
    c("Adult", "Weekend", "Day"),
    c("Senior", "Weekday", "Day"),
    c("Senior", "Weekend", "Day"),
    c("Junior", "Weekday", "Day"),
    c("Junior", "Weekend", "Day"),
    c("Adult with cart", "Weekday", "Day"),
    c("Adult with cart", "Weekend", "Day")
  )
  for (field in fields) {
    front <- one_price(facility, "Front 9", field[[1]], field[[2]], field[[3]])
    back <- one_price(facility, "Back 9", field[[1]], field[[2]], field[[3]])
    if (!identical(front, back)) {
      stop(facility, " front and back nines differ on ", field[[1]], ".", call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
for (facility in c("Kellogg", "Madison", "Newman")) same_walking(facility)

twilight_label <- function(facility, product) {
  day <- one_price(facility, product, "Adult", "Weekday", "Twilight")
  weekend <- one_price(facility, product, "Adult", "Weekend", "Twilight")
  if (!identical(day, weekend)) {
    stop(facility, " ", product, " twilight differs by day.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (is.na(day)) "—" else money(day)
}
nine_twilight <- function(facility) {
  front <- twilight_label(facility, "Front 9")
  back <- twilight_label(facility, "Back 9")
  if (front == "—" && back == "—") {
    "—"
  } else if (front == "—" ) {
    paste("Back 9", back)
  } else if (back == "—" || front == back) {
    front
  } else {
    paste("Front", front, "/ Back", back)
  }
}
row_of <- function(facility, product, label, twilight) {
  data.frame(
    Course = facility,
    Product = label,
    Adult = money(one_price(facility, product, "Adult", "Weekday", "Day")),
    Senior = money(one_price(facility, product, "Senior", "Weekday", "Day")),
    Junior = money(one_price(facility, product, "Junior", "Weekday", "Day")),
    `Weekday with cart` = money(one_price(facility, product, "Adult with cart", "Weekday", "Day")),
    `Weekend with cart` = money(one_price(facility, product, "Adult with cart", "Weekend", "Day")),
    Twilight = twilight,
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
peoria <- rbind(
  row_of("Kellogg", "Executive 9", "Executive 9", twilight_label("Kellogg", "Executive 9")),
  row_of("Kellogg", "18 holes", "18 holes", twilight_label("Kellogg", "18 holes")),
  row_of("Kellogg", "Front 9", "9 holes", nine_twilight("Kellogg")),
  row_of("Madison", "18 holes", "18 holes", twilight_label("Madison", "18 holes")),
  row_of("Madison", "Front 9", "9 holes", nine_twilight("Madison")),
  row_of("Newman", "18 holes", "18 holes", twilight_label("Newman", "18 holes")),
  row_of("Newman", "Front 9", "9 holes", nine_twilight("Newman"))
)
knitr::kable(
  peoria,
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Peoria walking fees, in dollars. Adult, senior, and junior are the same on weekdays and weekends. Nine-hole rows use the front nine, which matches the back nine except for twilight."
)
```

A cart is $17 on 18 holes and $12 on nine holes. A pull cart is $5, and one club is $1. Club rental is $20 at Kellogg 18 and Newman 18, and $10 on the other products. On a weekday, adult-with-cart equals the walking fee plus the cart. On Kellogg Executive and Madison Back 9, twilight is above the daytime walking fee. On Kellogg Back 9 it is $20, below the $30 daytime fee. Junior twilight, military, and the holiday 18-hole rate with a cart are empty columns. The holiday header is May 11 through September 29.

The extract has no quoted price, so this page does not estimate how rounds respond to a rate. The synthetic section in [Weather and playable capacity](weather-and-elasticity.html) checks a known equation. It does not use this guide.
